newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end with losses dragged down by banks.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end with losses dragged down by banks.

text.p: Greek equities opened firm but retreated quickly to close off lows at 961.35 points succumbing to selling pressure in the leading banking sector, brokers said. Other sectors showed also weakness.
"Banks, the locomotive of the Athens bourse, lost ground today driving the benchmark index lower," Yannis Kalogerakis, head of trading at ABN AMRO Axias Securities, told Reuters.
"Prospects are good but I do not expect much before the new government's policy statements and the 1997 draft budget," said kalogerakis.
Prime Minister Costas Simitis will make a speech on his government's economic policy on October 10 in parliament.
The Athens general share index closed 0.45 percent, or 4.31 points lower at 961.35 from Wednesday's 965.66 close after opening at 966.38 points.
Turnover stood at 9.29 billion drachmas on volume of 3.60 million shares boosted by block trades in Titan, Alpha Credit Bank and ErgoBank.
Gainers traced decliners 66 to 141 with 35 issues unchanged on 242 traded. Banks lost 0.48 percent, industrials fell 0.41 percent and construction tumbled 1.76 percent. Small-caps fell 0.66 percent.

Greece's new socialist cabinet was sworn in last week with Yannos Papandoniou elevated to economic "czar", heading both the national economy and finance ministries. The socialists have a comfortable 162-seat majority in the 300-seat parliament.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 554-572 at the close. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, ended up five drachmas at 4,080.

The recently launched Merrill Lynch stock index call warrant based on a basket of 23 shares was higher at 201.20-211.80 drachmas. It expires on January 9 1998 with a strike price of 1000. It was in the money at 1050.4.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 4,602-4,883 drachmas at the close. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
